name: Teo Halvorsen
field: film school and an AI startup for filmmakers
line: Is in his final year at a film school far from his family and is the solo founder of an AI tool that builds a first assembly cut for editors.

project.title: Cutlist
project.logline: An AI tool that logs raw footage and builds a first assembly cut for an editor to start from, in beta with thirty-eight editors.
constraints: The accelerator application is due in nineteen days, so only work that changes the application counts.
Runway is eleven weeks, so every cost is stated per hour of footage.
He is the only founder, and works at night around the thesis short.

statements.text: He is building Cutlist, an AI tool that cuts a first assembly from raw footage, and has an accelerator application due in nineteen days.
He prefers one input and one button to a settings page.
He would rather cut a scene by a third than add a shot to explain it.
He likes a reply to open with the problem, never with praise.
He wants blunt answers with no hype.
He wants the answer first and the reasons after it, in under eighty words.

preferences.text: He wants a demo clip with captions and no voice-over.
He would take a single plain word as a feature name over a descriptive phrase.
He wants music added only after the picture is locked.

new_work: My beta users keep asking for a free plan. Do I give them one before the application goes in, or hold the line on charging per hour of footage?
The thesis short is two minutes over the festival's limit and every scene feels necessary. How do I decide what goes?
A possible cofounder wants a long call before she will commit to a build weekend. What do I say to move it along?
